step: STEP 4 - redesign the ACCEPTANCE RULE for proposals
decision_rule: If the retrained model's recall@D=5 is below pm_v10's 83.7% (TP@D=5 < 901), then steps 4 and 5 are recorded DEAD-BY-EVIDENCE and are NOT attempted.
reason: A redesigned admission rule only pays off when a high-recall proposal source exists whose proposals are worth admitting. The re-baselined OBB detector produces TP@D=5 234 vs pm_v10's 901, i.e. it finds 667 FEWER true boxes than the shipped pipeline - so there is no proposal surplus to rescue. S5 had already shown the gate was binding at 311-of-936 admitted proposals, but that was with the pre-GT checkpoint whose '97.7% recall' was measured against Compare-V1; on the true GT the proposer itself is the limiting factor, not the gate.
caveat: The retrain was compute-capped (300 images / 8 epochs / 384 px / yolov8n-obb) because a 20-epoch 640 px yolov8s run projected at ~8 h on CPU and was killed at the goal's 90-minute cap. ~56k labelled real images exist (Label@CARS_202609_raw, 62218 json files, ~141k boxes), so this verdict is 'dead at this compute budget', not a refutation of the DL path. See benchmark/loop2_pseudo_labels.json :: corpus_inventory.
note: Recorded per Done-when #5 (unattempted steps must carry a measured reason, never an unexplained skip).
